Subject: Convenience unwind and notice cadence — MSA/Order Form redlines

Hi Alex / Laura,

Thanks again for the redline window. Our legal team flagged two items in the MSA + Order Form that we need to align on before we can proceed to procurement: 

1) Auto-renew + notice window: Acme is uncomfortable with a short auto-renew notice for enterprise agreements. We typically ask for a 90-day notice for cancellation for convenience on enterprise-tier deals.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC): Our counsel wants clearer hand-off obligations and data escrow triggers on a TFC — specifically a defined data export SLA and presence of an escrow if Redwood is sunsetting a hosted model.

Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on: 1) increasing the notice window for enterprise deals and 2) the offboarding/export SLA tied to TFC? If you have an internal playbook or suggested wording, please share so we can speed legal review.

Also copying EMEA Legal (legal@acme-corp.com) to keep the thread consolidated. We have procurement kickoff next Tuesday; ideally this closes before then.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Partnerships, Acme Corporation

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Convenience unwind and notice cadence — MSA / Order Form redlines

Tom — thanks for the clear note. Appreciate the heads-up on procurement timing. High-level reply and proposed path below; attached is a redline with suggested language and a draft order form with the offboarding SLA callouts.

Summary of Redwood position / proposal:
- Auto-renew notice: We can accommodate a longer enterprise notice window for Acme — propose 60 days for standard enterprise and 90 days for deals above $1M ARR or with cross-border data residency requirements. This gives Redwood some runway while meeting Acme's governance needs.
- Termination for convenience: We are OK to add a defined offboarding/export SLA (30 days for data export + 90 days for full access to historical logs) and a data escrow trigger if Redwood discontinues the model variant that Acme relies on.
- Escrow: We typically do escrow as an enterprise add-on; to avoid deal delay we can include a conditional escrow clause in the MSA and finalize the escrow vendor in the Order Form.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I've attached Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf with concrete clause language (see §7.2 — Termination & §12 — Data Access / Escrow).
2) Draft OrderForm-Acme-Draft.xlsx includes a Tier-based notice table and a checkbox for escrow/advanced offboarding services.
3) Laura / Ben — can you confirm commercial impact if we accept 60-day (standard) / 90-day (high-value) split? If not, propose counter language.

If that approach is acceptable to Acme Legal, I'll ask Legal to sign off on the redline and we can push the final to DocuSign this week.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Looping in my suggested legal posture. I reviewed Alex's redline and have two adjustments before we send to Acme Legal: 

- For enterprise deals tied to core product integrations (where data portability risk is material) we should default to 90-day notice. For the rest, 60 days is acceptable.
- The offboarding SLA: we can commit to a 30-day export period for live exports, but insist on a 90-day archival retrieval window (we will need a small fee if retrieval is required after 90 days). This protects our engineering schedule.

Commercial ask for Ben: If we roll the 90-day default for core integrations, what is the expected impact on redemptions / churn assistance budget? We need a quick check to confirm there's no material pricing change required.

Tom / Acme legal — if that split (90-day for core + 60-day standard) looks workable, we'll update the Order Form to call out which SKUs/training/integrations are considered 'core' and will mark the escrow option as "available" for signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick commercial check from my side: good to accept the 60/90 split as Laura suggested with two clarifications on billing/offboarding costs:

- No change to list pricing. We should not bake a price increase into the MSA for the 90-day notice; treat it as part of enterprise terms.
- Offboarding fee: agree to the 30-day export window + 90-day archival retrieval period. After 90 days, archival retrieval will incur a one-time retrieval fee (we'll define in the Order Form). For customers with higher-than-expected egress, we'll flag for a surcharge (standard practice).

Operational ask: Alex — please add the offboarding SLA bullets to the OrderForm-Acme-Draft.xlsx and flag any SKUs that meet Laura's "core integration" definition. Laura — happy to approve redline language once those SKUs are listed so we can close with procurement.
